question: Can knowledge without vibration explain agency even in the highest subject?
premises: Knowledge entirely without vibration is not admissible, even for Śiva.
The opponent treats the triad as an instrument of agency.
An instrumental account still does not show the self as the true agent.
inference: Therefore, redefining agency through a vibrationless triad fails to establish real agency.
uncertainties: The reading śarvasyāpi follows the transmitted text; some editions may normalize the name differently.
plain_english: A knowledge without vibration would not be possible even for Śiva, and merely having knowledge, desire, and effort has been described only as an instrument, not as true agency.
